title: The evolving liquidity landscape − speech by Victoria Saporta
summary: Victoria Saporta, Executive Director for Markets at the Bank of England, delivered a speech at the ECB Money Market Conference 2025 examining how central bank balance sheet normalisation, higher global government bond issuance, and expanding NBFI footprint are reshaping the liquidity environment. She discussed the interplay between these factors and their implications for monetary control and financial stability, noting that sterling reserves have decreased by approximately £322bn since QT began in February 2022.
key_points: Bank of England began balance sheet unwinding in February 2022; sterling reserves have decreased by approximately £322bn through QT and TFSME repayments
STR and ILTR facilities currently supply £152bn of reserves, up from approximately £12bn in January 2024
Bank of England's Preferred Minimum Range of Reserves (PMRR) is estimated at £375-540bn based on counterparty surveys
ILTR minimum spread for Level A collateral increased from 0 to 3 basis points to balance incentives between STR and ILTR facilities
Overnight General Collateral gilt repo rates spiked to over 30 basis points above Bank Rate recently due to TFSME repayments coinciding with month-end
Central banks globally are targeting equilibrium reserve levels between pre-GFC and peak-QE levels during normalisation
why_it_matters: This speech provides critical insights into how the Bank of England's demand-driven repo-led operating framework functions as reserves normalise. Market participants need to understand the mechanics of the STR and ILTR facilities as primary tools for supplying reserves and anchoring short-term rates to Bank Rate. The increase in ILTR spreads and potential for temporary repo rate spikes are operationally important for money market traders, dealers, and any entity managing short-term liquidity or collateral.
market_structure_context: The speech directly addresses market structure by examining the evolution of liquidity infrastructure: how central bank balance sheet normalisation interacts with increased government bond issuance and NBFI participation to reshape repo market dynamics. The BoE's elastic reserve supply framework is positioned as essential for anchoring short-term rates while the transition to PMRR creates structural frictions that can cause temporary repo rate spikes. The STR facility allows unlimited reserves against Level A collateral (gilts) at Bank Rate, while the ILTR supplies reserves weekly for six months against broad collateral.
important_numbers: 0 to 3 basis points (ILTR Level A collateral spread change)
30 basis points above Bank Rate (recent repo rate spike)
